new_statements.rule_in_words: Capell tentatively suggests that stress is contrastive (lexical) in Nagarige (= Piva/Lawunuia) on the strength of one near-minimal pair from his 1963 survey vocabulary (ˈvisuna 'his nose' vs viˈsuna 'her breast'), but immediately notes that in the Amun dialect of the same language the pair differs segmentally (vi-ˈisuna vs viˈsuuna, i.e. an extra vowel / vowel length), and concludes only that the languages need further study. No placement rule is given. (For the sister language Banoni, Lynch & Ross 2002:441 give penultimate stress on vowel-final words, final on consonant-final words, with phonemic vowel length, which would make Capell's pair a length contrast rather than a stress contrast; nothing equivalent has been published for Piva itself.)
new_statements.exceptions: The Amun dialect forms (vi-ˈisuna / viˈsuuna) are presented by Capell himself as counter-evidence to a stress analysis.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms (possessed nouns with 3sg suffix -na) from a survey wordlist; word level. Capell treats Nagarige and Amun as dialects of 'Banoni'; both are Lawunuia (lawu1237) varieties in current classification.
new_statements.identity_note: Capell (1971) calls the variety 'Nagarige' (with a northern enclave dialect 'Amun') and treats both as dialects of Banoni; Glottolog/OLAC list Nagarige, Naghareghe, Piva and Amun as names of Lawunuia (lawu1237, ISO tgi), distinct from Banoni proper (bano1247, ISO bcm). The only explicit stress RULE in print (penultimate on V-final words, final on C-final words; Lynch & Ross 2002:441) is for Banoni (bano1247), not Lawunuia, and should not be transferred without a Piva-specific source.
